meaning: A picture works if it shows the elements' real data readably and truthfully: values in the right places, marks you can see, elements you can identify, and no text that contradicts what is drawn.

items.why: The bars start at the atomic mass instead of the melting point, so they climb steadily across the table; the names overlap into an unreadable pile and the subtitle's '0 never measured' is false.
Each element's melting-to-boiling interval sits at its correct kelvin values in its CPK colour, with a room line, labelled axis, legend and honest handling of sublimation and unmeasured elements.
There is no title or axis labels, and near-black marks on a dark ground show a meaningless rising staircase instead of the liquid intervals.
A readable, correctly scaled liquid-interval chart in atomic-number order, with bromine and mercury called out at the room line and the unmeasured superheavies left as faint stubs.
Pixel-identical to W04: correct intervals, clear room line, and bromine and mercury properly called out.
The data and layout are the same as W04, and Br and Hg are highlighted on the axis, but the callouts only say 'liquid' where they should name the two elements, which is weaker.
